q: The EIA Notification in India under the Environment (Protection) Act was first issued in:
solution: The EIA Notification in India was first issued in 1994 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The purpose of this notification was to evaluate the environmental consequences of proposed projects before they were granted approval. It mandated that certain projects, like mining and thermal power plants, required prior clearance and a submission of an Environmental Impact Assessment report.

q: A construction firm generates 12 tons of Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste per day. If the project operates for 26 days in a given month, what is the total monthly waste generation, and does the firm qualify as a "Bulk Waste Generator" under the C&D Waste Management Rules, 2016?
options: 312 tons; Yes, because the monthly generation exceeds 300 tons.
312 tons; No, because the daily generation is less than 20 tons.
300 tons; Yes, because it meets the exact threshold.
240 tons; No, because it falls below both daily and monthly thresholds.
solution: Under the Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste Management Rules, 2016, a "Bulk Waste Generator" is defined as any enterprise/project generating 20 tons or more in one day OR 300 tons or more per project in a month. Calculation: 12 tons/day \(\times\) 26 days = 312 tons/month. Even though the daily generation (12 tons) is less than 20 tons, the monthly total (312 tons) exceeds the 300-ton threshold, classifying them as a Bulk Waste Generator.

q: Which of the following is NOT included during Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)?
options: A detailed assessment of the planned project and selected alternative compared to the baseline conditions.
Qualitative description measuring higher, medium and low impacts.
Quantitative description measuring physical values of water withdrawal, sewage produced and pollutants released.
All the data collection, analysis and developed plans summarized together in a well- structured and concise document.
solution: because while the Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) is indeed the summary document, the process of EIA includes the assessments described in A, B, and C.

q: What is the purpose of an Environmental Impact Statement?
options: To promote the project to investors
To document the findings of the EIA process
solution: The primary purpose of an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) is to provide detailed information on a proposed project's potential environmental, social, and economic consequences, enabling informed decision-making and promoting environmentally responsible development. The EIS serves as a tool for government agencies to evaluate projects, a means to inform the public, and a platform for public comment and participation in the decision-making process.

q: What is the first step in developing an Environmental Management Plan?
solution: Sequence: The Environmental Management Plan (EMP) is the document that details how the environmental impacts of a project will be managed. Therefore, one cannot develop the EMP without first identifying those impacts. The Process: EIA (Assessment): Identifies potential impacts and baseline conditions. Mitigation (Planning): Designing measures to reduce impacts (part of EMP). Monitoring (Execution): Tracking the effectiveness (part of EMP).

q: Which regulatory framework is commonly referred to in the development of an EMP?
solution: The most commonly referenced regulatory framework for developing an EMP is the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 in India, which mandates Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) and EMPs for projects needing environmental clearance from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC).

q: Following option international standard is most commonly associated with EMS?
solution: The international standard most commonly associated with Environmental Management Systems (EMS) is ISO 14001. ISO 14001 provides the framework for organizations to design, implement, and continually improve their EMS to enhance environmental performance, comply with legal and regulatory requirements, and achieve environmental objectives.

q: When conducting an environmental aspect evaluation, an EMS should consider factors including:
options: Resource use, emissions, and waste generation.
Legal requirements with scientific not assessment.
solution: When conducting an environmental aspect evaluation for an Environmental Management System (EMS), an organization should consider factors including resource use, emissions, and waste generation.

q: As per the rules, who is responsible for collecting the user fee for solid waste management from households and establishments?
options: The waste collector or the local body
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
solution: The responsibility for collecting the user fee for solid waste management from households and establishments lies with the waste collector or the local body. The CPCB, Ministry, and SPCB are regulatory and policy-making bodies and are not responsible for the on-ground collection of user fees.

q: The SWM Rules, 2016, specify that non-recyclable inert waste having a calorific value of more than 1500 Kcal/kg should be used for which purpose?
options: Incineration in a dedicated waste-to-energy plant
solution: The SWM Rules specify that non-recyclable inert waste with a high calorific value (more than 1500 Kcal/kg) should be used as fuel in a dedicated waste-to-energy plant to reduce the volume of waste going to landfills and generate energy.

q: As per the rules, the responsibility of a street vendor for the waste they generate ends with which action?
options: Paying a user fee to the local body.
Segregating the waste and handing it over to the designated waste collector.
Disposing of the waste in the nearest public dustbin.
Paying a spot fine if found littering.
solution: The responsibility of a street vendor for the waste they generate ends with segregating the waste and handing it over to the designated waste collector. Paying a user fee does not absolve them of this duty, and disposing of waste in public dustbins is not the correct protocol for bulk waste from vendors. Paying a fine is a consequence of non-compliance, not a fulfillment of their responsibility.

q: What is the mandatory time frame for a local body to provide a solid waste collection service to every household and commercial establishment in its area?
options: Within 12 months from the date of the rules' notification
Within 18 months from the date of the rules' notification
Within 24 months from the date of the rules' notification
No specific time frame is mentioned
solution: The SWM Rules do not specify a mandatory time frame for a local body to provide solid waste collection services to every household and establishment.

q: During the preparation of an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report for a proposed industrial facility, the noise impact of two heavy crushers must be evaluated. If Crusher A produces a noise level of 80 dB and Crusher B produces a noise level of 80 dB, what is the combined noise level that must be reported for environmental clearance?
solution: Noise levels (measured in decibels) are logarithmic and cannot be added algebraically. The formula for adding two identical noise sources is: \(L_{total} = L_1 + 10 \log_{10}(n)\) , where n is the number of identical sources. Calculation: \(L_{total} = 80 + 10 \log_{10}(2)\) . Since \(\log_{10}(2) \approx 0.301\) , the addition is 80 + 10(0.3) = 80 + 3 = 83 dB.

q: The SWM Rules also apply to "Special Economic Zones." Who is the designated authority responsible for implementing the rules in these zones
options: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry
The developer of the Special Economic Zone
solution: The SWM Rules, 2016, specify that for Special Economic Zones (SEZs), the designated authority responsible for implementing the rules is the developer of the zone.

q: A municipality is seeking Environmental Clearance (EC) for a new sanitary landfill. The EIA study projects that the facility will receive 100,000 tonnes of municipal solid waste annually. If the waste is compacted to a density of 800 \(kg/m^3\) and the State Pollution Control Board restricts the maximum depth of the waste to 10 meters to protect the aquifer, what is the minimum active landfill area required per year? (Assume 1 tonne = 1000 kg and ignore daily soil cover volume).
solution: Step 1: Convert mass to kilograms. \(\text{Total Mass} = 100,000 \text{ tonnes} \times 1000 \text{ kg/tonne} = 100,000,000 \text{ kg}\) Step 2: Calculate the required volume. \(\text{Volume} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}} = \frac{100,000,000 \text{ kg}}{800 \text{ kg/m}^3} = 125,000 \text{ m}^3.\) Step 3: Calculate the required area. \(\text{Area} = \frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Depth}} = \frac{125,000 \text{ m}^3}{10 \text{ m}} = 12,500 \text{ m}^2.\) Step 4: Convert square meters to hectares \((1 \text{ Hectare} = 10,000 \text{ m}^2). \text{Area} = \frac{12,500}{10,000} = 1.25 \text{ Hectares}.\)

q: Which of the following is considered a "bulk waste generator" under the rules, based on the quantity of waste generated per day?
options: A residential society generating more than 10 kg
A commercial establishment generating more than 20 kg
A hostel or hotel generating more than 50 kg
solution: Under the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2016 , and the updated SWM Rules, 2026 , a "bulk waste generator" is primarily defined as any entity or establishment that generates an average of more than 100 kg of waste per day from all waste streams combined.

q: According to the PWM Rules, 2016, what is the minimum thickness mandated for plastic carry bags at the point of manufacture and import?
solution: The Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, increased the minimum thickness of plastic carry bags to 50 microns. This was a significant step to ensure a higher value for the bags, making them more likely to be collected and recycled.

q: The concept of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) in plastic waste management makes which entity financially responsible for the waste generated by their products?
options: The producer, importer, and brand owner
solution: The EPR framework places the financial and organizational responsibility for the management of post-consumer plastic waste on the producers, importers, and brand owners who introduce the products and packaging into the market.

q: The PWM Rules mandate that brand owners must register with which authority?
options: The Central or State Pollution Control Board
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry
solution: Brand owners, under their EPR obligation, are required to register with either the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) or the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB), depending on their scale of operation.

q: The rules specify a minimum thickness for carry bags. This rule does not apply to which of the following?
options: Plastic films used for food wrapping
Plastic bags made from recycled material
solution: The rule regarding the minimum thickness of plastic carry bags does not apply to compostable plastic bags. Compostable bags are regulated under a different set of rules that require them to conform to specific standards for composability.

q: Which of the following single-use plastic items is NOT covered under the nationwide ban?
solution: The ban on single-use plastics covers items that have low utility and high littering potential. Multi-layered plastic (MLP) pouches for milk and other food products are not on the list of banned items. They are, however, subject to EPR regulations.

q: The rules prohibit the use of plastic sachets for which specific product?
solution: The use of plastic sachets for pan masala, gutkha, and tobacco is strictly prohibited under the PWM Rules.

q: Under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016, which of the following is a key responsibility of a producer under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)?
options: Providing financial assistance to local authorities for waste collection.
Ensuring that e-waste is channelled to an authorized dismantler or recycler.
Setting up municipal solid waste processing facilities.
Conducting public awareness campaigns about general waste disposal.
solution: The core of EPR is to make the producer responsible for the end-of-life management of their products. This includes ensuring that the e-waste is collected and channeled to an authorized recycler or dismantler to prevent informal and illegal recycling.

q: What is the correct term for the system established by a producer to ensure the collection of e-waste from consumers, as per the rules?
solution: The E-Waste Rules specifically use the term "take-back system" to describe the method through which producers are required to collect their e-waste from consumers.

q: The E-Waste Rules prohibit the use of certain hazardous substances in the manufacture of EEE. What is the maximum concentration value by weight in homogeneous materials for lead, mercury, and hexavalent chromium?
solution: The E-Waste Rules mandate that the maximum concentration value by weight for hazardous substances like lead, mercury, and hexavalent chromium in homogeneous materials should not exceed 0.1%.

q: Who is responsible for providing the necessary infrastructure for the collection of e-waste from their designated collection points?
solution: Under the EPR framework, the producer is responsible for establishing a collection system and providing the necessary infrastructure for the collection of their e-waste.

q: What is the minimum penalty for a producer who fails to meet their EPR targets, as per the rules?
options: A fine of up to ₹1 lakh
A fine of up to ₹5 lakh
A fine calculated as a percentage of their turnover
No specific minimum penalty is mentioned
solution: The E-Waste Rules do not specify a minimum penalty for a producer who fails to meet their EPR targets. Penalties are determined based on the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, which provides for a general framework of penalties.

q: What is the mandatory time limit within which bio-medical waste must be treated and disposed of from its generation, as per the rules?
solution: To prevent health hazards, all bio-medical waste must be treated and disposed of within 48 hours of its generation.

q: A "Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facility" (CBWTF) is licensed for what purpose?
options: To transport and store bio-medical waste.
To collect, transport, treat, and dispose of bio-medical waste for multiple healthcare facilities.
To audit and monitor the waste management practices of hospitals.
solution: A CBWTF is a facility that is licensed to provide a comprehensive service for multiple healthcare facilities, including the collection, transport, treatment, and final disposal of their bio-medical waste.

q: What is the correct protocol for the disposal of solid, liquid, or gaseous waste from a bio-medical incinerator?
options: It should be disposed of in a common landfill.
It must comply with the emission and discharge standards specified in Schedule III of the rules.
It must be handed over to a common hazardous waste treatment facility.
solution: The waste from a bio-medical incinerator must be managed according to the strict emission and discharge standards laid out in Schedule III of the rules.

q: Which of the following color-coded bags is used for the disposal of discarded and contaminated linen, beddings, and dressings?
solution: According to the Biomedical Waste Management Rules (standardized in many regions, including India), the Yellow Bag is specificall y designated for highly infectious and soiled waste

q: Which of the following is considered "liquid bio-medical waste"?
solution: Laboratory wastes, such as cultures and stocks of infectious agents, are a category of liquid bio-medical waste.

q: What is the primary objective of "transboundary movement" rules for hazardous waste?
options: To facilitate the export of hazardous waste for disposal in other countries
To regulate the import and export of hazardous waste for recycling and recovery
To ensure that hazardous waste is always disposed of within the country of its origin
To encourage illegal trade in hazardous waste
solution: The primary objective is to regulate and control the transboundary movement of hazardous waste, primarily for recycling and recovery purposes, while preventing illegal traffic.

q: Which of the following is NOT required for the transport of hazardous waste?
options: A valid authorization from the SPCB
Proper packaging and labelling as per the rules
A no-objection certificate from the local police
solution: A no-objection certificate from the local police is not a requirement for the transport of hazardous waste under the rules.

q: What is the primary purpose of a "Construction and Demolition Waste Management Plan"
options: To secure financial approval for a project
To detail how the waste will be segregated, stored, and managed on-site
To obtain a license from the local municipality
To list all the contractors and subcontractors
solution: A C&D Waste Management Plan is a mandatory document that provides a roadmap for how the waste generated from a project will be segregated, stored, and managed on-site before being transported to a processing facility.

q: The rules state that a local authority can collect a "tipping fee" for the waste it processes. What does this fee cover
options: The cost of transporting the waste
The cost of final disposal in a sanitary landfill
The cost of segregation and recycling
solution: The tipping fee is collected by a local authority or a C&D waste processing facility to cover the cost of the final disposal of inert waste in a sanitary landfill.

q: What is the mandatory minimum percentage of the new batteries a producer sells that they must collect back for recycling in the first year of their operation?
solution: According to updated guidelines, the mandated recovery rate for battery materials starts at 70% in the 2024-25 fiscal year , increasing to 80% by 2026, and 90% from 2026-27 onwards

q: The rules were recently amended to incorporate which new type of batteries under the EPR framework?
solution: The recent amendments to the Batteries (M&H) Rules brought used electric vehicle (EV) batteries under the EPR framework, given the increasing adoption of electric vehicles.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognized method of solid waste disposal?
solution: Open dumping is a prohibited and illegal method of solid waste disposal due to the severe environmental and health hazards it poses. Landfilling, incineration, and composting are all recognized and regulated methods for managing solid waste.

q: A "Waste Management and Handling Plan" is a requirement for whom?
options: All waste generators, as per their respective rules
solution: A "Waste Management and Handling Plan" is a requirement for all waste generators as per their specific waste management rules (e.g., C&D Waste Rules, E-Waste Rules).

q: The "Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)" framework is based on which of the following principles?
solution: The EPR framework is a practical application of the Polluter-Pays Principle, as it makes the producer financially and organizationally responsible for the pollution caused by their products.

q: The concept of "resource efficiency" in waste management refers to:
options: The use of fewer resources to produce the same amount of goods.
The efficient use of waste as a resource.
The efficient collection and transportation of waste.
The efficient disposal of waste in a landfill.
solution: Resource efficiency is a key goal of sustainable development. It refers to using fewer resources to produce the same amount of goods, thereby reducing waste generation.

q: hat is the full form of the term "CPCB "
solution: The full form of CPCB is Central Pollution Control Board.

q: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, provides for penalties for non-compliance with the rules. What is the maximum imprisonment for a person who violates any rule?
solution: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, provides for a maximum imprisonment of five years for a person who violates any rule.

q: What is the core principle of "Integrated Solid Waste Management"?
options: The disposal of all waste in a single, large landfill
A comprehensive approach combining source reduction, recycling, and disposal
The management of waste by a single government authority
The use of a single technology for all types of waste
solution: Integrated Solid Waste Management is a comprehensive approach that combines various methods, including source reduction, recycling, composting, and disposal, to manage waste effectively.

q: The concept of "Life Cycle Assessment" in waste management refers to
options: The environmental impact of a product from "cradle to grave"
The durability and reusability of a product
The cost of a product's disposal
solution: Life Cycle Assessment is an evaluation of a product's environmental impact from the extraction of raw materials ("cradle") to its final disposal ("grave").

q: What is the first and most preferred option for the management of hazardous waste, as per the hierarchy in the rules?
solution: As per the hierarchy, recovery, recycling, and reuse are the most preferred options for hazardous waste management, before treatment or disposal.

q: Under these rules, "co-processing" of hazardous waste is permitted. What does co-processing refer to?
options: Mixing hazardous waste with non-hazardous waste for disposal.
The use of hazardous waste as a raw material or fuel substitute in industrial processes, such as in cement kilns.
Jointly managing waste with another waste generator.
A process to chemically neutralize hazardous waste
solution: "Co-processing" is a waste management technique where hazardous waste is used as a raw material or a fuel substitute in industrial processes, most commonly in cement kilns.

q: What is the correct protocol for the disposal of solid, liquid, or gaseous waste from a bio-medical incinerator?
options: It should be disposed of in a common landfill.
It must comply with the emission and discharge standards specified in Schedule III of the rules.
It must be handed over to a common hazardous waste treatment facility.
solution: The waste from a bio-medical incinerator must be managed according to the strict emission and discharge standards laid out in Schedule III of the rules.

q: Which category of bio-medical waste is to be disposed of in a yellow bag with a label indicating the "type of waste"?
solution: Human anatomical waste is to be disposed of in a yellow bag with a label indicating the "type of waste," as this waste must be incinerated and handled with specific precautions.

q: Who was recently appointed as the brand ambassador of FICCI FRAMES?
solution: Ayushmann Khurrana was recently appointed as the brand ambassador of FICCI FRAMES.

q: Which player of the Indian women's cricket team was appointed as DSP in UP Police?
solution: Jhulan Goswami, a prominent player of the Indian women's cricket team, was appointed as Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) in the Uttar Pradesh (UP) Police.

q: Which state is at the top of the Fiscal Health Index Report 2025, recently released by NITI Aayog?
solution: According to the Fiscal Health Index Report 2025 by NITI Aayog, Odisha is at the top.

q: Who inaugurated the All India Campaign 'Our Constitution, Our Respect'?
solution: Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar inaugurated the All India Campaign 'Our Constitution, Our Respect'.

q: Which Indian Navy ship conducted the hydrographic survey of Mauritius recently?
solution: INS Sarvekshak conducted the hydrographic survey of Mauritius.

q: What is the reason behind bats flying in the dark?
options: They have a perfect vision in the dark.
They produce high-pitched sounds called ultrasonics.
solution: Bats use a process called echolocation. They produce high-pitched ultrasonic sounds and listen to the echoes to navigate and locate prey in the dark.

q: Which of these is the small-scale industry in India?
solution: Handloom Industry is a small-scale industry in India, while the others are generally considered large-scale.

q: At which place on earth are there days and nights of equal length always?
solution: At the Equator, the sun's rays are always perpendicular, resulting in approximately 12 hours of day and 12 hours of night throughout the year.

q: The largest public sector undertaking in the country is?
solution: Indian Railways is the largest public sector undertaking in India, in terms of employment and assets.

q: What is the full form of DRDL?
options: Department of Research and Development Laboratory
solution: The full form of DRDL is Defence Research and Development Laboratory.

q: Who is known as the 'father of Indian missile technology'?
solution: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is widely known as the 'father of Indian missile technology' for his work on the development of ballistic missile and launch vehicle technology.

q: Which of the following microorganisms causes diseases like polio and chicken pox?
solution: Polio and chicken pox are caused by viruses.

q: What is commonly known as 'white plague'?
solution: Tuberculosis is commonly known as 'white plague' due to its symptoms, particularly the pallor and wasting of the body.13

q: Which organ is the main digester and absorber of food?
solution: · Primary Function: While the stomach begins the process of breaking down proteins, the Small Intestine is the site where 90% of digestion and absorption occurs. · Mechanism: Digestion: It receives bile from the liver and enzymes from the pancreas to fully break down proteins, fats, and carbohydrates. Absorption: The inner walls are lined with millions of tiny finger-like projections called villi , which vastly increase the surface area to absorb nutrients directly into the bloodstream. · Other Options: Stomach: Primarily churns food and starts protein digestion. Colon (Large Intestine): Mainly absorbs water and electrolytes. Liver: Produces bile but food does not pass through it.

q: A gold ring which is 50% pure. Its purity can be alternatively shown as __:
solution: · Calculation: The purity of gold is measured on a scale of 24. 24 Karat = 100% pure gold. Therefore, 50% purity = 0.50 × 24 = 12 Karat. · Spelling Distinction (Karat vs. Carat): Karat (K): A unit of purity for gold (e.g., 24K, 18K). Carat (ct): A unit of weight for gemstones (e.g., a 1-carat diamond). Note: While "Carat" is sometimes used for gold in British English, when both options are present in a technical exam, Karat is the specific term for purity.
